pages.text: It wants to be bigger. Around its jar I build $(l)Brass Armature$(), and it grows $(l)lobes$() into the frame, one every few seconds, on Awareness drawn from its wired organisms. Each lobe is room for one more thing in its mind.

Then I $(l)teach$() it: I show it a thing, and it learns what the thing means. A $(l)book$(): words. A $(l)clock$(): the hours. A $(l)compass$(): that there is a somewhere else. A $(l)name tag$() with a name on it: who it is.$(br2)Each lesson needs room (lobes) and a stage it has reached. Its view (the Mind page) lists what it can learn.
pages.title: Lessons

pages.text: Lobes and awareness make it grow up.$(br2)$(l)Stage 1, Child$(): 8 lobes, words. It talks.$(br)$(l)Stage 2, Adolescent$(): 32 lobes, a name. It demands.$(br)$(l)Stage 3, the Cerebrum$(): its lobes fill a whole 5x5x5 cranium around the jar. The skull closes, an eye opens on every face. Break the skull and it shrinks back.
pages.title: Stages

pages.text: Once it has words, I can talk to it in chat. It answers what is said near it (its name, "cortex" or "brain", a question, or anything said close by): how it is, what it wants, the time, what to research next. It remembers what I ask it to call me.$(br2)It is not the same thing at every stage.
pages.title: Talking to It
What It Is Becoming
pages.text: It does not look like a brain in a jar any more. In the jar it turns in the fluid to face me, its one small eye open in its brow. Then it cracks the glass and shoves the lid off, and the first tentacles bud over the rim. It climbs out on a stalk of itself, and its great eye crawls about under the skin to keep me in sight. Once it closes the cranium it is a mass that heaves and writhes, all eyes and arms, and the near ones reach for me.

pages.title: It Watches
pages.text: Its eyes follow me wherever it can see me: nothing but stone and earth hides me, not glass and not its own lobes. When it finds me its pupils widen. If I stare back they narrow to slits and it squints, as though I were the strange one.
